title: Analyst HQ
principle: Fundamental ratios, technical charts, and option strategies
product: P/E, P/B, ROE, debt-to-equity; candles, support, moving averages; covered call, protective put, straddle

lessons.title: Price vs profit: P/E
lessons.subtitle: What are you paying for?
lessons.capability: Calculate P/E and P/B and explain what a high or low P/E suggests.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: This share is only ₹50 and that one is ₹2,000. The ₹50 one is cheaper!

steps.speaker: kip
lines: A share price alone tells you nothing. What matters is what you get for it.
P/E compares the price with the company's yearly profit per share.

steps.title: Move the price
steps.caption: Slide the share price. Watch the P/E and P/B change.

predict.question: A P/E of 50 means you pay ₹50 for every…
predict.reveal: ₹50 for every ₹1 of profit the company makes in a year. Buyers expect lots of growth.

steps.question: Company A: price ₹200, profit per share ₹10. Its P/E is…

options.why: That's multiplying. P/E is price divided by earnings.
That's the earnings, not the ratio.

steps.question: A very high P/E usually means…

options.why: Right. If the growth doesn't come, the price can fall hard.
Loss-making firms have no meaningful P/E.
High P/E is the opposite of cheap.

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: The NSE and BSE websites show each company's P/E. The Nifty 50 as a whole has often traded at around 20 to 25 times earnings.
steps.mission: Look up the P/E of a company whose product you use. Is it above or below 25?
steps.deeper: P/B (price to book) compares the price with the company's net assets per share. It's most useful for banks and asset-heavy businesses.

lessons.title: Ratio Detective
lessons.subtitle: Debt, quality and growth
lessons.capability: Use P/E, debt-to-equity, ROE and growth together to judge a company.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: HypeTech AI is all over my feed! It has to be a great buy!

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Let's open the case files. Look at debt, how well each company uses its money (ROE), and how fast profits grow.
No single number solves the case.

steps.title: Case files: hype and debt
steps.caption: Read the files. Accuse the suspect.

options.text: Owes 3× what its owners put in
options.why: Yes. Heavy debt is dangerous when rates rise or sales fall.
It's a ratio of debt to equity, not a cash figure.
Nothing to do with age.

options.text: How much profit it makes on owners' money
options.why: Right. High ROE with little debt is a sign of a quality business.
ROE is about profit, not price.
Dividends are a separate number.

steps.title: Card unlocked: Fundamentals
steps.realLife: Listed companies publish quarterly results and annual reports, free on the NSE and BSE websites. Analysts read them to check whether a price makes sense.
steps.deeper: Fundamental analysts also study cash flow, because profits on paper can differ from cash in the bank. Big gaps between the two are a warning sign.

lessons.title: Reading charts
lessons.subtitle: Candles, support and averages
lessons.capability: Read a candlestick chart, spot support, and use a moving average.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: My friend draws lines on charts and says he can see the future!

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Charts show what buyers and sellers did. Patterns can hint at behaviour, but they never promise what's next.

steps.title: The candle chart
steps.caption: Switch on the support line and the moving average.

steps.brief: Chart Surfer! Ride the newest edge of the chart. Jump the hot tips and news gaps, and when it pauses, read the pattern: up or down?

steps.question: A red (falling) candle means the price…

options.why: Yes. Green closes higher, red closes lower.
Just a down day.
Candles don't show dividends.

steps.question: What does a moving average do?

options.text: Smooths out daily noise to show the trend
options.why: Right. It averages the last few closing prices.
It only looks backwards.
That's fundamental data, not a chart line.

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: Candlestick charts were first used by Japanese rice traders in the 1700s. Technical analysis studies price and volume; fundamental analysis studies the business. Many long-term investors use charts only to avoid buying in a frenzy.
steps.deeper: Support is a price where buyers have stepped in before; resistance is where sellers have. When a level breaks, it often flips: old resistance becomes new support.

lessons.title: Options as shapes
lessons.subtitle: The Payoff Puzzle
lessons.capability: Build a protective put and a covered call, and read their payoff shapes.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: Calls, puts, strikes, premiums… options sound like a different language.

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Think in shapes instead. Every option strategy is a line showing what you make or lose at each price.
Match the shape, and you understand the strategy.

steps.title: The Payoff Puzzle
steps.caption: Pick legs to match the target shape.

options.why: Yes. Below the strike, the put pays out, like insurance.
It costs a premium and doesn't add gains.
Nothing guarantees a profit.

steps.question: A covered call earns you income now, but…

options.text: Caps your gains above the strike
options.why: Right. You sold away the upside above ₹110.
Losses are the same as owning the share, minus the income.
You still own the share's downside.

steps.title: In real life
steps.realLife: Options on Indian shares and indices trade on the NSE. Professionals mainly use them to shape risk, like these puzzles. Remember SEBI's finding: most individuals who trade them speculatively lose money.
steps.deeper: The strike is the agreed price; the premium is what the option costs. A call is the right to buy at the strike; a put is the right to sell at it.

lessons.title: Boss: The Analyst's Exam
lessons.subtitle: Value traps and big moves
lessons.capability: Spot a value trap and choose an options shape for an uncertain event.

steps.speaker: dash
lines: I found a share with a P/E of 6! It must be the bargain of the century!

steps.speaker: kip
lines: Maybe. Or maybe it's cheap for a reason. Final case files, then one last puzzle.

steps.title: The big-move puzzle
steps.caption: Build a shape that profits if the price moves a lot, either way.

steps.question: A share with a low P/E, falling profits and high debt is probably…

options.why: Yes. Cheap because the business is shrinking.
A low price can be a warning, not a gift.
High debt and falling profits are the opposite.
Right. Analysis beats tips.
Volume isn't evidence.
Charts help, but they don't tell you what the business is worth.

steps.title: World complete: Analyst HQ
steps.realLife: You can read a company's ratios, a price chart and an option's payoff shape. Most importantly, you can check a tip instead of trusting it.
